Solve(x == x, x), a tautology true for every x, answers {} (no solutions) for us -- the opposite of correct, since x==x holds for ALL x. Wolfram's {{}} means "one solution branch, no constraints" (any x). A real Solve edge-case bug for identically-true equations, not scoped to fix safely here.

Solve(..., Element(x, Complexes)) ignores the domain restriction entirely and returns only the real roots ({1,-1,Sqrt(2),-Sqrt(2)}), missing the four complex roots (+-I, +-I*Sqrt(2)) Wolfram includes. Our Solve has no domain-aware root widening/filtering machinery at all -- a real, substantial feature gap, not a self-contained fix.

Same root cause as eq-0 (Solve ignores Element(x, Domain) entirely): this Reals-restricted case happens to match Wolfram's real roots by coincidence since we never filter by domain in the first place, not because domain restriction is implemented.

Same root cause as eq-0: Solve(..., Element(x, Integers)) still returns the irrational roots +-Sqrt(2) alongside the integer ones, since the domain restriction is never applied -- here it's over-inclusive rather than under-inclusive.
No domain given, so Wolfram defaults to Complexes and returns all 4 roots; we default to reals-only and drop the 2 complex ones. Same missing domain-awareness as the other quartic Solve rows.

Missing the non-real roots (+-I) for the same reason as the other quartic rows; also collapses the repeated real roots to one occurrence each rather than keeping the multiplicity Wolfram's list shows. Same domain-awareness gap, compounded by no multiplicity tracking.
